rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī treats a former wife's mother as a stepdaughter: a man divorced her daughter before consummation still may not marry her.
rows.anchor: في رجل تزوج امرأة فطلقها قبل أن يدخل بها، أيتزوج أمها؟ قال: «هي بمنزلة الربيبة»

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd reportedly disliked marrying the mother if the wife died and he inherited from her, but allowed it after divorce before consummation.
rows.anchor: إذا ماتت عنده، وأخذ ميراثها، كره أن يخلف على أمها، وإذا طلقها قبل أن يدخل بها، فإن شاء فعل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the requirement of consummation applies both to mothers of wives and to stepdaughters.
rows.anchor: أن مجاهدا قال له: {وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم من نسائكم} [النساء: 23] أريد بهما الدخول جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the view that mothers-in-law are unconditionally forbidden: unlike stepdaughters, their prohibition is not qualified by consummation; he also cites consensus.
rows.anchor: والقول الأول أولى بالصواب، أعني قول من قال: الأم من المبهمات؛ لأن الله لم يشرط معهن الدخول

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says marrying a woman forbids her mother whether or not the daughter was entered, while marrying and divorcing an unconsummated mother leaves her daughter lawful.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إذا نكح الرجل المرأة فلا يحل له أن يتزوج أمها، دخل بالابنة أم لم يدخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī notes a flaw in the Prophetic report's chain, but says the consensus supporting the rule makes that report unnecessary as proof.
rows.anchor: وهذا خبر وإن كان في إسناده ما فيه، فإن في إجماع الحجة على صحة القول به مستغنى عن الاستشهاد

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Asked about a man who married but did not see or have intercourse with his wife before divorcing her, ʿAṭāʾ says her mother remains forbidden to him.
rows.anchor: الرجل ينكح المرأة لم يرها، ولا يجامعها حتى يطلقها، أيحل له أمها؟ قال: «لا هي مرسلة»

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A report records ʿAṭāʾ's answer to whether Ibn ʿAbbās read an added consummation qualifier after mothers of wives: «لا تبرأ».
rows.anchor: قلت لعطاء: أكان ابن عباس يقرأ: «وأمهات نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن» ؟ قال: «لا تبرأ»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabāʾib is the plural of rabība, a man's wife's daughter, named for his raising her; the form derives from marbūba shifted to rabība.
rows.anchor: وأما الربائب فإنه جمع ربيبة وهي ابنة امرأة الرجل، قيل لها ربيبة لتربيته إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wife's husband may also be called the rabīb of her son, with the relation expressed through paired forms such as rāʾib/rabīb and jābir/jubayr.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال لزوج المرأة: هو ربيب ابن امرأته، يعني به: هو رابه، كما يقال: هو جابر وجبير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains dukhūl here as intercourse, expressed in the report as nikāḥ.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن} [النساء: 23]

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A different interpretation makes dukhūl exposure: the bride is brought, uncovered, and the man sits between her legs; doing this at her family's home has the same effect and bars her daughter.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: قلت لعطاء، قوله: {اللاتي دخلتم بهن} [النساء: 23] ما الدخول بهن؟ قال: «أن تهدى إليه

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says uncovering a slave woman and sitting between her legs likewise makes her mother and daughter forbidden.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء: «إذا كشف الرجل أمته وجلس بين رجليها أنهاه عن أمها وابنتها»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's interpretation of dukhūl as intercourse: ordinary seclusion alone does not forbid the daughter, so the relevant access is sexual.
rows.anchor: وأولى القولين عندي بالصواب في تأويل ذلك، ما قاله ابن عباس، من أن معنى الدخول: الجماع والنكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says “from your loins” distinguishes naturally born sons from adopted sons.
rows.anchor: لأن معناه: وحلائل أبنائكم الذين ولدتموهم دون حلائل أبنائكم الذين تبنيتموهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says a son’s wife becomes forbidden by contract whether or not the marriage was consummated.
rows.anchor: عليها النكاح، دخل بها أو لم يدخل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wives of sons by suckling are equally forbidden; “from your loins” distinguishes biological sons from adopted sons, rather than excluding foster sons.
rows.anchor: إن حلائل الأبناء من الرضاع، وحلائل الأبناء من الأصلاب سواء في التحريم

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports that the verse was said to have been revealed when Muhammad married Zayd ibn Ḥāritha's former wife and polytheists criticized it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قلت لعطاء، قوله: {وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم} [النساء: 23] قال: «كنا نحدث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says God relieved people and did not burden them beyond their capacity.
rows.anchor: الفرائض وخفف عنهم فلم يحملهم فوق طاقتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception concerns unions already contracted before the ban; God forgives those who had joined sisters before its prohibition if they thereafter obey and avoid it.
rows.anchor: يخبر بذلك جل ثناؤه أنه غفور لمن كان جمع بين الأختين بنكاح في جاهليته وقبل تحريمه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical command addresses people claiming belief while resorting to false judges: they would not kill themselves or migrate from home in obedience, except a few.
rows.anchor: ولو أنا فرضنا على هؤلاء الذين يزعمون أنهم آمنوا بما أنزل إليك المحتكمين إلى الطاغوت أن يقتلوا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the addressed people as Jews and Arabs, comparing the command to the order given to Moses's companions.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله تعالى: {ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم} [النساء: 66] هم يهود يعني: والعرب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid specifies that Moses's companions were ordered to kill one another with daggers; only a few would have obeyed this command.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم} [النساء: 66] كما أمر أصحاب موسى

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī gives an occasion: Thābit ibn Qays and a Jewish man boasted that they would obey a command to kill themselves; the Jew said his people had done so, and the verse followed.
rows.anchor: عن السدي: {ولو أنا كتبنا، عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق السبيعي
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq reports that after the verse, a man said they would obey if commanded and thanked God for sparing them; the remark reached the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق السبيعي، قال: لما نزلت

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said some men of his community have faith more firmly rooted in their hearts than towering mountains.
rows.anchor: فبلغ ذلك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , فقال: «إن من أمتي لرجالا الإيمان أثبت في قلوبهم من الجبال الرواسي»

rows.speaker: نحويي البصرة
rows.claim: Some Basran grammarians parse قليل as a nominative substitute for the implicit subject of فعلوه, since those people perform the act.
rows.anchor: فكان بعض نحويي البصرة يزعم أنه رفع قليل لأنه جعل بدلا من الأسماء المضمرة في قوله: {ما فعلوه}

rows.speaker: نحويي الكوفة
rows.claim: Some Kufan grammarians explain the nominative through ellipsis and repetition: “they did it—only a few did it.”
rows.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: إنما رفع على نية التكرير، كأن معناه: ما فعلوه ما فعله إلا قليل منهم

rows.speaker: عمرو بن معد يكرب
rows.claim: A line by ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib supplies a poetic parallel for the exception construction: all brothers part, except the two stars.
rows.anchor: كما قال عمرو بن معد يكرب: [البحر الوافر]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers explaining nominative قليل by the sense “only a few did it”: it is an exception from the people previously described, after a negated act.
rows.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب أن يقال: رفع القليل بالمعنى الذي دل عليه قوله: {ما فعلوه إلا قليل منهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Syrian codices read قليلا in the accusative; this is also valid Arabic when the verb is occupied by a pronoun referring back to the previously mentioned group.
rows.anchor: وهي في مصاحف أهل الشام: «ما فعلوه إلا قليلا منهم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exhortation is obedience to God and compliance with His command; doing so benefits people in this world and the next and makes them firmer and more steadfast.
rows.anchor: طاعة الله والانتهاء إلى أمره {لكان خيرا لهم} [آل عمران: 110] في عاجل دنياهم وآجل معادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrites act doubtfully, so their deeds vanish; acting with insight would earn reward and lasting merit with God and strengthen their faith in His promise.
rows.anchor: المنافق يعمل على شك، فعمله يذهب باطلا، وغناؤه يضمحل فيصير هباء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī glosses أشد تثبيتا as confirmation: belief strengthens the person and makes resolve more sound.
rows.anchor: عن السدي: {لكان خيرا لهم وأشد تثبيتا} [النساء: 66] قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī points to the parallel phrase about spending for God's pleasure and seeking inner confirmation, whose explanation he has discussed elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وهو نظير قوله جل ثناؤه: {ومثل الذين ينفقون أموالهم ابتغاء مرضاة الله وتثبيتا من أنفسهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For obedience, God would give a great reward, strengthen resolve and judgment, and help the obedient carry out their deeds.
rows.anchor: يعني بذلك جل ثناؤه: {ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به لكان خيرا لهم} [النساء: 66] لإيتائنا إياهم على فعلهم ما وعظوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is the unbending way, God's upright religion chosen and prescribed for His servants: Islam; هدينا means “We granted them success” in following it.
rows.anchor: يعني: طريقا لا اعوجاج فيه، وهو دين الله القويم الذي اختاره لعباده وشرعه لهم، وذلك الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transitions from the promised guidance to the enduring honor and elevated ranks God promises those who obey Him and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر جل ثناؤه ما وعد أهل طاعته وطاعة رسوله عليه الصلاة والسلام من الكرامة الدائمة لديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe affirm God's oneness and what He sent with Muhammad, and hold fast to the clear light revealed to His Prophet.
rows.anchor: وتمسكوا بالنور المبين الذي أنزل إلى نبيه

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses “hold fast to Him” as holding fast to the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج: {واعتصموا به} [النساء: 175] قال: «بالقرآن»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy rescues them from punishment and secures reward and Paradise; His grace brings them what He gave the believers who affirmed His messengers.
rows.anchor: فسوف تنالهم رحمته التي تنجيهم من عقابه وتوجب لهم ثوابه ورحمته وجنته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God enables them to attain His favor and guides them to follow the path and example of those He blessed through obedience.
rows.anchor: ويسددهم لسلوك منهج من أنعم عليه من أهل طاعته، ولاقتفاء آثارهم، واتباع دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is God's approved religion for His servants, Islam.
rows.anchor: وذلك هو الصراط المستقيم، وهو دين الله الذي ارتضاه لعباده، وهو الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, صراطا is accusative by separation from the pronoun in إليه.
rows.anchor: ونصب الصراط المستقيم على القطع من الهاء التي في قوله {إليه}

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: One interpretation takes شعائر الله as God's inviolable limits, commands, prohibitions, and obligations; ʿAṭāʾ glosses them as sacred bounds, avoiding divine displeasure, and following obedience.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء، أنه سئل عن شعائر الله، فقال: حرمات الله: اجتناب سخط الله

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies God's signs here with the sanctuary of God.
rows.anchor: عن السدي: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحلوا شعائر الله} [المائدة: 2] قال: " أما شعائر الله: فحرم الله "

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes the signs as the rites of pilgrimage, the markers of the bounds God set for Hajj.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: {لا تحلوا شعائر الله} [المائدة: 2] قال: «مناسك الحج»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that Muslims wanted to attack pagan pilgrims who visited the sanctuary, sacrificed, honored its sacred sites, and traded during pilgrimage; God forbade violating the signs.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا لا تحلوا شعائر الله} [المائدة: 2] قال: " كان المشركون يحجون البيت الحرام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid lists Ṣafā and Marwa, sacrificial offerings, and camels among God's signs.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {شعائر الله} [البقرة: 158] الصفا والمروة

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: A further interpretation says not to make lawful what God has prohibited during consecration.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: معنى ذلك: لا تحلوا ما حرم الله عليكم في حال إحرامكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains God's signs as things God forbade a person in consecration from touching.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {لا تحلوا شعائر الله} [المائدة: 2] قال: " شعائر الله: ما نهى الله عنه أن تصيبه وأنت محرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers ʿAṭāʾ's broad reading: do not violate God's sacred limits or neglect obligations. Since signs are markers of what God made known, the wording covers all divine boundaries, rites, commands, prohibitions, and lawful and forbidden things; its general form cannot be restricted without proof.
rows.anchor: وأولى التأويلات بقوله: {لا تحلوا شعائر الله} [المائدة: 2] قول عطاء الذي ذكرناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not make the sacred month lawful for fighting the polytheists; al-Ṭabarī links the prohibition with the question about fighting in a sacred month.
rows.anchor: ولا تستحلوا الشهر الحرام بقتالكم به أعداءكم من المشركين، وهو كقوله: {يسألونك عن الشهر الحرام قتال فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command as not permitting fighting in the sacred month.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولا الشهر الحرام} [المائدة: 2] يعني: لا تستحلوا قتالا فيه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says that because polytheists were not then barred from the House, Muslims were ordered not to fight in the sacred month or at the sanctuary.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: كان المشرك يومئذ لا يصد عن البيت، فأمروا أن لا يقاتلوا في الشهر الحرام ولا عند البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī identifies the sacred month here as Rajab of Muḍar, when Muḍar prohibited fighting; he notes a competing view that it is Dhū al-Qaʿda and refers to his earlier argument.
rows.anchor: وأما الشهر الحرام الذي عناه الله بقوله: {ولا الشهر الحرام} [المائدة: 2] فرجب مضر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima offers the alternative identification of the sacred month as Dhū al-Qaʿda.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن عكرمة، قال: هو ذو القعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says not to prevent the offering from being brought to the place God appointed for it at His Kaʿba.
rows.anchor: أن يبلغوا به المحل الذي جعله الله محله من كعبته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says an offering is hady so long as it has not been garlanded, and describes one vowed as an offering and garlanded.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولا الهدي} [المائدة: 2] قال: «الهدي ما لم يقلد، وقد جعل على نفسه أن يهديه ويقلده»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī introduces the question of what the prohibited garlands are, then reports several interpretations.
rows.anchor: ثم اختلف أهل التأويل في القلائد التي نهى الله عز وجل عن إحلالها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view distinguishes ungarlanded offerings as الهدي from garlanded ones as القلائد; Ibn ʿAbbās says garlanding an offering places the man in consecration, so he must remove his shirt.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولا القلائد} [المائدة: 2] القلائد: مقلدات الهدي، وإذا قلد الرجل هديه فقد أحرم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says pagan pilgrims wore garlands of samur bark while traveling to Mecca and hair on the return, and people left them unharmed.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة: {لا تحلوا شعائر الله ولا الشهر الحرام} [المائدة: 2] قال: «كان الرجل في الجاهلية إذا خرج من بيته يريد الحج تقلد

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another reported view says people wore garlands when leaving the sanctuary, using bark from its trees to secure safety from Arab tribes.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل كان الرجل منهم يتقلد إذا أراد الخروج من الحرم أو خرج من لحاء شجر الحرم
